area_note: Extremely small, area-optimized core. The entire 32x32 register file is just 1024 flops; adding a 16-word (512-bit) internal state buffer to a custom instruction is massive and consumes half as much area as the CPU's main architectural state.
constraints: The coprocessor interface (PCPI) cannot access memory; it has no memory address or data ports.
Memory operands must be loaded into registers by standard CPU instructions before a custom instruction can use them.
An instruction can read at most two 32-bit registers (rs1, rs2) and write at most one 32-bit register (rd).
Custom units cannot operate in the background concurrently with CPU execution; the CPU stalls in the fetch/decode state until pcpi_ready is asserted.
coprocessor: Pico Co-Processor Interface (PCPI). Receives the 32-bit instruction and two 32-bit register values (rs1, rs2). Wait and ready signals control pacing.
coprocessor_result: A single 32-bit value (pcpi_rd) and a write-enable signal (pcpi_wr).
custom_opcode_space: Any opcode not recognized by the base RV32I decoder triggers instr_trap and is forwarded to the PCPI (e.g., standard custom-0 to custom-3 spaces).
evidence: picorv32.v module parameters (COMPRESSED_ISA, ENABLE_MUL, ENABLE_DIV) dictate the ISA.
cpu_state state machine (cpu_state_fetch, cpu_state_ld_rs1, cpu_state_exec) proves the multi-cycle, non-pipelined microarchitecture.
pcpi_* ports in the top module lack any memory address or data signals, proving no memory access.
pcpi_rd and pcpi_wr are the only output data ports from the PCPI interface back to the CPU.
assign instr_trap catches all non-base opcodes and routes them to the PCPI.
isa: RV32I with optional C (Compressed) and M (MUL/DIV) extensions, configurable via parameters.
memory_interface: Simple 32-bit valid/ready handshake (mem_valid, mem_ready, mem_addr, mem_wdata, mem_wstrb, mem_rdata).
microarchitecture: Multi-cycle state machine (not pipelined). An ALU instruction takes ~4 cycles (fetch, decode/read, exec, writeback). A load takes ~6 cycles.
name: PicoRV32
